name: SN74LV1T125DBVR
title: Single-supply buffer with 3-state output and lowered input thresholds, CMOS logic level shifter
summary: One non-inverting CMOS buffer with an active-low output enable, in a five-lead SOT-23 (DBV) or SC70 (DCK), running from 1.6 V to 5.5 V. Its input switches at lowered thresholds and takes up to 5.5 V at any supply, so one part moves a signal up (1.8 V to 3.3 V at VCC = 3.3 V) or down (5 V to 3.3 V at VCC = 3.3 V). The output swings to VCC and ground, drives up to 8 mA at 5 V, and goes high impedance with OE high. Rated from -40 °C to 125 °C.

operation.text: With OE low, Y repeats A: high in, high out; low in, low out. With OE high, Y goes high impedance whatever A is. OE is not to be left floating, as the output may oscillate.

The output swings to the VCC rail and to ground, so the supply chosen sets 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V or 5 V CMOS levels; the output is compatible with the AUP1G and LVC1G families. Output drive is 8 mA, a level set to reduce line reflections, overshoot and undershoot.

The input thresholds are lowered below standard CMOS. At a 5 V supply a standard CMOS input needs 3.5 V for a high; this part needs only 2 V, so a 2.5 V signal can drive a 5 V output. With VCC = 3.3 V, a 1.8 V input is read as high. A high input stays above VIH(MIN), a low one below VIL(MAX). Driving a high-impedance load, the output sits near VCC when high and near 0 V when low.

The input takes up to 5.5 V at any VCC in range, so a higher-voltage signal comes out at the VCC level: 5.0 V, 3.3 V or 2.5 V logic into a 1.8 V system with VCC = 1.8 V, for one. A high input lies between VIH(MIN) and 5.5 V, a low one below VIL(MAX).

The input is high impedance and is modelled as a resistance across the input capacitance. Edges must cross between valid levels within the input transition rate of the recommended operating conditions; slower edges raise supply current and can make the output oscillate. An input that is not always driven gets a pull-up or pull-down; 10 kΩ usually meets every need.
No input is left floating, as an undefined level gives an undefined state. Each unused input is tied high or low, usually to VCC or GND, whichever suits the logic function or the layout.

The output has clamp diodes to both VCC and GND; the inputs have a clamp to GND only. Input and output voltages may go past the absolute maximum ratings only while the clamp currents stay within their ratings.

The output stage is balanced CMOS push-pull: source and sink currents are about equal. Edges into a light load are fast, and routing and loading affect ringing. The stage can deliver more current than it withstands, so output power stays inside the absolute maximum electrical and thermal ratings. An unused push-pull output is left unconnected.

VCC is any value inside the recommended range. A 0.1 µF bypass capacitor goes on VCC as near the pin as possible; several in parallel can cover different noise frequencies, 0.1 µF with 1 µF being common.
Characterized up to 50 MHz with VCC = 3.3 V. Latch-up performance is above 250 mA per JESD 17. Inputs tolerate 5.0 V. The pinout is the standard logic one.
An AEC-Q100 qualified automotive version is the SN74LV1T125-Q1.

All orderable parts are MSL level 1 at 260 °C peak reflow. DBV follows JEDEC MO-178, DCK JEDEC MO-203; DCK lead width falls outside JEDEC. Body sizes leave out mold flash, protrusions and gate burrs, which add at most 0.25 mm per side. The middle lead on the pin 4 to 5 side is a support pin that may differ or be absent.
